Hello there!

I won't lie, this feels really weird, for various reasons. Not only is this my first post on this new, but strangely familiar website, but it is also my first time as a mod. I really have no idea what to expect. What I'd like to hope is that I'll look back on this with my piles of money and fifty girlfriends and laugh about how much of a young naive whelp I was all those days ago, but my biggest hope is that this actually goes anywhere at all. Like, maybe a couple people laugh; that would be neat.

For a bit of a boring biography, my name is IAmTheWii and I am a mod of v/DiYRemix. Nothing else really has happened to me yet, but I'll keep you informed. In regards to this subverse's inspiration, it began when I discovered the speed option on YouTube videos. Since it was 3a.m. and I was an idiot, I decided to listen to "It Will Rain" at 2X speed. I immediately fell in love. All of a sudden, songs that I couldn't stand were completely different, and songs that I loved were near unrecognizable. I'm not sure if this kind of subverse has been made on that other site, but I decided to make it here after <insert political drama here>.

Anyways, I hope you enjoy this humble subverse, and before I free you from this way too long introduction, a word of advice: listen to the original songs before the remixes. Even if you hate them, or find them lame, your brain will thank you for it. I know this from experience; as a young child, I for some reason listened to my Billy Joel's The Stranger LP at 72 rpm, it ruined the album for years.

Happy Remixing,

TheWii

I used to be an avid user of Deaddit for 4 years before I jumped ship almost 5 month ago. That website was my main daily browsing routine. I simply fell in love with the concept of a community curating content in community categorized subjects and filtering it all using up/down votes. I spent 3 years contributing within that community with posts and comments accumulating points north of 10k in both. Like all communities, it had its share of trolls, spammers, bigots, etc. but it also had some of the most educated, thoughtful, and resourceful people I have ever met.

It is really a sad sight seeing a once beautiful creation tumbling down.

But life goes on, and now I'm on Voat and I'm loving it even more. And I promise that I will happily carry the responsibility to be a useful contributor to this platform that provides me with my daily doze of pleasure.

Thank you Voat and thank you everyone for being such awesome people :)
